title: Early Career Accelerator and Systems Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook describes the Redwood Early Career Accelerator (ECA): a combined program and system of tooling designed to accelerate new joiner impact, reduce time-to-productivity for junior ICs, and create durable, transparent pathways from IC1/IC2 to IC3. It covers program structure, tooling and access flows, role checkpoints, mentorship pairings, and measurable success criteria.

Scope
- New joiners with 0–4 years experience (graduating students, apprentices, bootcamp hires).
- Cross-functional scope: Eng, Product, Design, Customer Success.
- Integrates People Ops systems (Greenhouse/HRIS), internal tools (Okta, GitHub, Jira, Slack), and learning platforms (Lattice Learn, internal content).

Principles
- Time-bound: clear milestones at Day 7, Day 30, Day 60, Day 90.
- Observable: measurable success metrics (ramp score, PR throughput, paired-review percentage).
- Low friction: automated provisioning where possible; manual steps documented and minimized.
- Equity-first: consistent assignment of mentors and opportunities across regions.

Program Owners and RACI
- Program owner: People Ops Early Careers (lead: Aisha Patel).
- Operational owner (access provisioning): IT & Security (owner: Miguel Ortega).
- Mentorship coordinator: Talent Enablement (owner: Rina Shah).
- Hiring manager: New hire’s direct manager (responsible for role onboarding and development).

RACI summary
- People Ops: Responsible for program curriculum and cohort scheduling.
- IT & Security: Account provisioning and MFA enforcement.
- Hiring Manager: Accountable for performance checkpoints and 1:1 cadence.
- Mentor: Consulted for weekly pairing and code reviews.
- New Joiner: Informed and owner of learning tasks.

Onboarding timeline and checklist (Day 0–90)
- Day 0 (Offer acceptance -> first day):
  1. Invite to Redwood Okta + SSO enabled by IT within 4 business hours.
  2. HR & Benefits orientation scheduled (via HRIS) and calendar invite sent.
  3. Pre-boarding learning bundle delivered (Lattice Learn + team-specific README).
- Day 1–7 (Foundations):
  1. Team kickoff: manager-run 90-day plan walkthrough.
  2. Access checklist: GitHub org, team repo access, Jira project role, Slack channels, internal wiki. Target SLA: 24 hours for GitHub, 48 hours for privileged infra access.
  3. Pairing: Mentor assigned and first 1-hour orientation pairing scheduled.
- Day 8–30 (Contribute safely):
  1. First small production task (bug fix or doc update) assigned and merged.
  2. Security training and code-of-conduct acknowledgement complete.
  3. First checkpoint: manager + mentor + new joiner triad meeting.
- Day 31–60 (Independent contributor):
  1. Ownership of a small feature or customer-facing task.
  2. Shadow rotations: 2 half-day shadow sessions with cross-functional partner.
  3. Midpoint review: documented feedback in Lattice and updated 90-day plan.
- Day 61–90 (Prepare for scaling impact):
  1. Demonstrated applied learning (feature shipped, customer bug resolved).
  2. Development plan set for next 6 months with at least two measurable goals.
  3. Graduation review: recommendation for continued growth track and suggested badges.

Access & Tooling Matrix (owners and typical SLA)
- Okta (SSO + groups): Owner: IT & Security, SLA: 4 business hours for standard groups.
- GitHub (org + repo roles): Owner: Eng Tools team, SLA: 24 hours for read/write; 72 hours for admin-level teams.
- Jira (project roles): Owner: Eng PMO, SLA: 48 hours.
- Slack (channels + user groups): Owner: Eng Tools, instant for basic channels; 24 hours for private group invites.
- AWS/GCP test accounts: Owner: Infra, SLA: 3 business days, requires manager approval.
- Vault/KMS access (if needed): Owner: Security, SLA: 5 business days and elevated approval flow.

Example provisioning table (text format)
| Artifact | Request channel | Approver | Typical SLA | Required Info |
| Okta group (engineer) | internal-requests@redwood | IT oncall | 4h | employee ID, team, start date |
| GitHub repo write | github-access@redwood | Repo owner | 24h | GitHub username, team, repo |
| AWS dev account | infra-requests@redwood | Infra lead | 3bd | cost center, manager approval |

Mentorship and Buddy System
- Pairing model: every ECA participant is assigned a mentor (senior IC or manager) and a peer buddy (same-level IC) for social onboarding.
- Weekly cadence: 1-hour mentor pairing the first 30 days, then 1x every 2 weeks until Day 90. Buddy check-ins daily first two weeks.
- Mentor responsibilities:
  - Run structured pairing sessions (checklist provided below).
  - Provide 3 concrete learning tasks within Week 2.
  - Give ongoing feedback, escalate blockers to hiring manager when needed.

Structured mentor pairing checklist (template)
1. Day 1: Orientation to team mission, tech stack, and coding standards.
2. Day 3–7: Live walkthrough of a simple bug and the deploy process.
3. Week 2: Pair on a small ticket from ideation to PR.
4. Week 4: Feedback session and career aspiration conversation.

Career ladders, micro-checkpoints and competencies
- Target levels covered by ECA: IC1 -> IC2. Program sets milestone competencies in three domains: Technical craft, Collaboration, and Product judgment.
- Example micro-checkpoints (all must be documented in Lattice):
  - IC1 (onboarding target): able to make a small, tested code change; follow review feedback; participate in standups.
  - IC1.5 (intermediate): owns recurring bug triage; writes clear unit tests; contributes to docs.
  - IC2 (graduation): owns a small feature end-to-end; independently carries customer context in tickets; mentors a peer.

Measurement and success criteria
- Ramp score (composite metric): PR merge rate, code review responsiveness, learning module completion, manager assessment. Goal: median ramp score >= 0.7 by Day 60.
- Retention: target 12-month retention >= 85% for cohort participants.
- Time-to-first-merge: target median <= 21 days.

Learning curriculum and content sources
- Core modules (hosted in Lattice Learn + internal wiki):
  - Redwood engineering fundamentals (codebase orientation).
  - Product & customer primer (top 5 customers and use-cases).
  - Security basics and compliance checklist.
  - Communication playbook: PR etiquette, async updates.
- Supplemental: Office hours with Platform SRE, once per sprint.

Manager playbook (first 90 days)
1. Create and agree on a 90-day plan in Week 1 and upload to Lattice.
2. Schedule recurring 1:1 twice per week for the first month, weekly thereafter.
3. Assign at least 2 meaningful reviewable tasks by Day 30.
4. Provide midline written feedback at Day 45 and final assessment at Day 90.

Operational automation and tickets
- Preferred automation flows:
  - New hire in HRIS triggers Okta account creation and an email to Eng Tools for GitHub/Jira provisioning (webhook-based).
  - If a provisioning SLA is missed, an automatic escalation ticket opens in PagerDuty to the relevant oncall rotation.
- Manual ticketing: use internal-requests@redwood with the provisioning template below.

Provisioning request template (copy into ticket)
- New hire name: 
- Role and team: 
- Start date: 
- Required repos/services: (list)
- Manager approver: (name and email)
- Justification for elevated privileges (if any):

Inclusion and equitable practices
- Mentors assignment rotates to ensure distribution across teams and minimize bias.
- Remote-friendly times: all cohort events scheduled with alternating time slots for APAC/EU/NA participants.
- Accessibility: all learning content includes captions, transcripts, and downloadable materials.

Budget and perks for ECA participants
- One-time equipment stipend: $1,200 (for home office essentials).
- Conference attendance: cohort members may apply for up to $1,500 within the first 12 months.
- Training credits: $300 per participant for paid learning content (Udemy, O’Reilly, etc.).

Escalations and recovery plan
- If a participant is at risk at Day 45 (based on ramp score < 0.4), manager opens an Individualized Support Plan (ISP) with People Ops.
- ISP steps: 2-week focused improvement plan, dedicated mentor hours (5–8 hours/week), weekly syncs with People Ops.
- If insufficient progress after 8 weeks, formal performance process begins per People Ops guidelines (link to policy).

How to adopt this playbook for a team (1-page checklist)
1. Assign a Team Lead for ECA participation (owner for provisioning and scheduling).
2. Reserve one senior mentor for every 4 cohort participants.
3. Confirm provisioning SLAs with Eng Tools and Security.
4. Publish team-specific first-90-day checklist in team wiki and link to this playbook.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Standard 90-day plan template (copyable to Lattice).
- Appendix B: Quick troubleshooting for common provisioning failures and remediation steps.
- Appendix C: Mentor feedback form (used at Day 30 and Day 90).

Contact and feedback
- Program owner: people-ops@redwood (Aisha Patel).
- Provisioning incidents: it-oncall@redwood (Miguel Ortega).
- Mentorship coordination and learning content: talent-enable@redwood (Rina Shah).

Change log
- 2026-02-15: Document created.

This playbook is intended to be a living document. Suggested improvements should be filed as feedback tickets to people-ops@redwood with subject line: "ECA Playbook Feedback".
